title: Unified lifecycle orchestrator for community weights: conversion, validation, and pin publishing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a single orchestrator component that takes community/open-source model weights from ingestion through deterministic conversion, runtime compatibility validation, and automated pin + performance-profile publication to the model catalog. This ticket covers the end-to-end workflow glue: staging area transfer, hermetic conversion runners, artifact signing and fingerprinting, a standardized smoke-and-profile suite (latency, throughput, basic quality checks), and a publish gate that creates an immutable pin with metadata consumed by Redwood Console and the hosted model catalog. The orchestrator must support parallel conversions, backpressure controls, and clear retry semantics so we can safely onboard high-volume community submissions without operator intervention. Scope excludes new UI surfaces; this focuses on backend automation and safe publish rules.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Orchestrator accepts an inbound signed manifest and copies artifacts to staging with provenance metadata (uploader, checksum, source URL)
A2: Conversion workers run in isolated containers and produce runtime artifacts (quantized shards, runtime config) reproducibly across two independent runs

A3: Validation suite executes deterministically and returns a standard profile JSON containing latency percentiles, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, KV cache correctness check, and a quality sanity score (BLEU/QA recall/LLM-eval quickset)
A4: Automated pin is created only when validation passes and a signature is stored; pin includes: model-semver, artifact-hash, conversion-matrix, profile-id, and recommended runtime flags
A5: Publishing workflow surfaces any failures with actionable remediation steps and creates a rollbackable candidate so ops can revert the pin in <15 minutes
A6: End-to-end observability (events, traces, and metrics) emitted to Console; sample dashboard shows per-model conversion latency and profile success rate
technical_notes: Use hermetic container images pinned by digest for conversion and quantization steps to ensure reproducibility
Fingerprint scheme: SHA-512 over canonicalized artifact tar + conversion params; store both fingerprint and sign with KMS key
KV cache correctness test: load model, run deterministic prefix sequences and verify token-by-token KV cache matches golden run within tolerance
Profile bucketized percentiles: p50/p90/p99 latency (per 1..2048 token lengths) and throughput under 1/4/16 batch sizes
Conversion workers must report resource hints (vram needed, ops kernel requirements) for scheduler to pick appropriate pool
implementation_plan: Stage 1 (week 1): design orchestrator API and staging schema; add manifest fields for provenance and conversion hints
Stage 2 (week 2): implement hermetic conversion runner service and local smoke-suite harness; add fingerprint + sign step
Stage 3 (week 3): integrate validation suite and profile generator; add publishing gate that writes pin to catalog and creates audit record
Stage 4 (week 4): add observability: events, tracing, and Console dashboard; run canary on 5 community models
Stage 5 (week 5): harden retry/backoff policies, finalize RBAC for private deployments, and request security review
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and fingerprint computation
Integration tests: full pipeline run against three representative OSS models (small, medium, large) in CI with mocked GPUs
Reproducibility test: run conversion twice on unique runner hosts and assert identical fingerprints
Load test: enqueue 100 submissions and confirm orchestrator respects concurrency limits and backpressure
Chaos test: kill a conversion worker mid-run and verify automatic restart and idempotent behavior
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): run pipeline on staging and onboard 5 vetted community models; monitor profile differences vs. baseline
Phase B (beta): allow select partner internal teams to request onboarding; expose read-only profiles in Console
Phase C (public): enable automated pin publishing for community submissions with rate limits and optional manual approval mode for flagged models
Rollback: pins are append-only; implement alias pointer per model that can be switched back to previous pin within 15 minutes via API
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: non-deterministic conversion producing different artifacts -> Mitigation: hermetic runners + canonicalization + retry and human audit
Risk: malicious model artifacts -> Mitigation: require signed manifests, run conversion in sandboxed VPC, and flag unknown ops for review
Risk: validation suite giving false negatives on quality -> Mitigation: separate fast sanity checks from deeper offline evals and mark profiles as provisional
Risk: high ingestion volume overwhelms conversion capacity -> Mitigation: token-based queueing, priority lanes for paid customers, and autoscale knobs
